subject: RFI: Tenancy containment and cross-zone invocation guarantees
messages:

Subject: RFI: Tenancy containment and cross-zone invocation guarantees

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick onboarding session earlier — Edison is moving this through procurement this week and our security team has one set of clarifying asks before we sign off. We need a compact packet that covers how Redwood prevents cross-tenant invocation and data leakage during: normal operation, model failover (cross-zone routing), and sidecar/agent upgrades. Specifically we want:

- A network diagram showing control plane vs dataplane boundaries (eg. tenant metadata flows vs inference traffic).
- A short threat model describing the top 3 cross-tenant attack paths you consider and mitigations.
- How sidecars enforce tenant isolation for invocation and KV cache access; are caches namespaced or global?
- Evidence we can hand to auditors: packet/flow logs, example ACLs, and a minimal canary test plan for failover.

Can you get us a one-page summary + diagram and a proposed date for a 45-min technical deep-dive? Procurement is on a tight timeline.

Appreciate it,
Tom

--

Subject: Re: RFI: Tenancy containment and cross-zone invocation guarantees

Tom — thanks for the clear asks. Attached are two artefacts: an updated isolation diagram (isolation_diagram_v2.png) and our control-plane/egress checklist (controlplane-egress-checklist.pdf). High-level summary below; I can join the deep-dive if you want the architecture team present (Rishi and Vanessa are cc'd).

Executive summary (two paragraphs)
Redwood enforces tenancy containment by splitting responsibilities: a customer-scoped control plane (metadata, scheduling, routing decisions) is logically separated from the dataplane (encrypted inference streams). Tenant identifiers are carried only in control-plane messages and in per-request mTLS cert SANs; the runtime enforces tenant boundaries in the dataplane via per-tenant namespaces, sidecar policies, and cache keying. During model failover we route by tenant tag and prefer in-region, capacity-isolated pools to avoid cross-tenant co-residency changes when possible.

Key controls (bullets)
- Control plane: tenant metadata stored in a customer-indexed datastore with strong RBAC; all scheduling decisions are logged and signed.
- Dataplane: mTLS between client-proxy -> sidecar -> runtime; each sidecar presents ephemeral certs scoped to tenant-id.
- Sidecar isolation: sidecars run in individual tenant sandboxes (container + network namespace). Network policies + eBPF filters restrict outbound hosts and ports per-tenant.
- KV cache: strictly namespaced by tenant-id (cache keys include tenant prefix + HMAC tag). We rotate HEKs (host encryption keys) on a schedule and support customer-managed KMS.
- Failover & routing: model-variant routing preserves tenant routing headers; if a variant is unavailable we fall back to a pre-approved compatible model in same tenancy tier, with audit logging and throttled queueing to prevent cross-tenant amplification.

Attachments & evidence links below; next steps: 1) confirm 45-min slot (suggest Dec 8 or 9), 2) we can provide a sample packet of anonymized flow logs under NDA and a sample canary runbook.

Attachments: isolation_diagram_v2.png (image/png), controlplane-egress-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-archifacts

Let me know which items you want in the auditor packet and we'll prepare.

Marissa — this is a great start, thanks. A couple of clarifying points from our security team:

1) During cross-zone model failover (e.g., zone A to zone B due to capacity), is there any window where two tenants could be co-resident on the same runtime worker with shared IPC or cache? If yes, how is data leakage prevented?
2) For the KV cache: can you show an example cache key format and the HMAC scheme? We're evaluating whether tenant scoping is robust against key collision or accidental prefix leaks.
3) Can you provide a stripped sample of flow logs (sufficient to show tenant-id tagging in the control-plane flow vs dataplane flow) and an outline of the canary plan (I want to present that to our SRE team).

If you can get those three items and a short paragraph on sidecar behavior during rolling upgrades (how long a sidecar can accept requests after a control-plane disconnect), we can close the security checklist.

Tom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ruiz <tr@edison-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@edison-health.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: Tenancy containment and cross-zone invocation guarantees

Tom — quick follow with the concrete answers you asked for below. Attaching a mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) that maps artifacts to audit owners. Also linking a short canary runbook in the Drive folder (see links).

1) Cross-zone failover co-residency: we avoid unnecessary cross-tenant co-residency by preferring capacity pools reserved per-customer where requested (Dedicated) and by preferring same-tenant-capacity variants for Hosted. Where co-residency is unavoidable (ephemeral spill to shared pools), the runtime enforces process-level separation and disallows shared IPC: the inference runtime does not expose shared memory segments between tenant processes; the sidecar/loader creates an isolated process namespace and enforces seccomp & cgroup limits. In addition, all KV cache entries are keyed with a tenant prefix + 64-bit HMAC (SHA256 truncated) derived from a HEK unique per-tenant-per-region. Example cache key: "tenant:<TENANT_ID>|v1|hmac:3f5b9a2c". This prevents accidental collisions and makes blind enumeration infeasible.

2) HMAC/keying: we use HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 64 bits, applied to (tenant_id || model_variant || sequence_prefix). HEKs are rotated on a 24-hour rolling window by default for Hosted (configurable) and are wrapped by the customer's KMS if requested. We can share a sample (anonymized) key-derivation excerpt under NDA.

3) Flow logs & canary: attached in Drive are a sanitized flow-log sample (no PII) showing separate control-plane RPCs carrying tenant metadata (request_id, tenant_id) and a separate dataplane capture where payloads are mTLS-protected and contain no tenant metadata. Canary plan: 5% traffic to canary pool, preflight ACL checks, accelerated telemetry baseline (latency/error thresholds) and abort/revert policy. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-archifacts

4) Sidecar rolling upgrades: sidecars accept in-flight requests for up to 30s after receiving a drain signal, continuing to serve only existing connections; new requests are routed to replacement sidecars. Control-plane disconnect triggers a short-lived local fallback where the sidecar will deny external-originated writes but continue to serve cached inference reads for a customer-scoped TTL (default 10s) to avoid data exposure outside tenant context.

Next steps: please confirm whether you want the anonymized flow logs packaged as CSV or PCAP for your auditors and which date/time you'd prefer for the 45-min deep-dive (we have open slots Dec 8 10:00-10:45 PT or Dec 9 14:00-14:45 PT).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,
